key_insight: Expanding Generative Flows and Expanding Flow Maps learn to generate outputs whose size can grow during the generation process, rather than assuming a fixed canvas or fixed sequence length.
engineering_relevance: This enables controllable variable-size generation for both continuous and discrete problems, including images, graphs, and sequences, with a unified flow-based framework.
method: Introduce an expanding interpolant that adds conditional noise to increase dimensionality over time.
Factor each map into an expand operator plus a transport map to jointly add dimensions and denoise.
Extend the construction to the discrete simplex for variable-size graph and sequence generation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports broad applicability across continuous and discrete modalities, with special cases recovering existing fixed-size flows and flow maps.
watch_item: Practical performance may depend on how well the expand operator is trained to add meaningful new coordinates or tokens without destabilizing the transport step.
